decisions.quote: We conducted a preregistered close replication and extension of Studies 1, 2, and 4 in Hsee (1998).
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding agree that the study is a replication testing Hsee (1998) with new data.

decisions.quote: Hsee, C. K. (1998). Less is better: When low-value options are valued more highly than high-value options. Journal of Behavioral Decision Making, 11(2), 107–121. https://doi.org/10.1002/(sici)1099-0771(199806)11:2
decisions.reason: Both the shipped row and blind target identify Hsee (1998) as the original study; the DOI printed in the paper's reference list is a truncated prefix of the full SICI DOI recorded in the shipped row.

decisions.quote: Overall, we found support for four of the five effects in Hsee (1998), with no support for the fifth effect, which was in the right direction (Table 5). Our extensions resulted in insightful findings. We conclude robust evidence for the less is better effect, with effect size varying when compared to the original, depending on the vignette used. However, there was weaker evidence for the more is better effect, with only Study 2 showing significant support for it.
decisions.reason: The authors explicitly present an overall mixed outcome across the five tested effects from Hsee (1998), confirming four effects (all three 'less is better' effects and the Study 2 'more is better' effect) while failing to replicate the Study 4 joint-evaluation 'more is better' effect.
